key_insight: Detonation-sprayed Ni–Cr–Fe–B–Si–C coatings require a trade-off between low friction and high wear resistance, controlled by barrel filling, gas ratio, and inter-shot delay.
engineering_relevance: Tuning these parameters can improve coatings for restoring and surface-strengthening machine components.
method: Varied barrel filling from 48–68%, working-gas molar ratio O/C from 1.026–1.856, and inter-shot delay from 0–1 s.
Evaluated coating morphology, friction, specific wear rate, roughness, and hardness.
evidence_signal: The minimum friction coefficient was 0.674 ± 0.136 at 48% filling and O/C = 1.026, while the highest wear resistance occurred at O/C = 1.856 with increased delay, reaching a specific wear rate of 0.000189 mm³/(N·m).
watch_item: Low-friction settings increased wear, and medium-to-high barrel filling promoted microcracks; parameter selection should prioritize the intended service conditions.
paper_title: Development of a Method for Producing Self-Fluxing Nickel-Based Coatings by Detonation Spraying
